title: Car Pooling
summary: Each trip is [passengers,start,end] along a one-way route.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–1000 trips. Each passenger count is in [1,100]. 0 ≤ start < end ≤ 1000. 1 ≤ capacity ≤ 100000.
contractDetails.output-checking: Compare a boolean feasibility result. Trips use half-open intervals [start,end), with drop-offs before pickups at a shared location.

statement: Each trip is [passengers,start,end] along a one-way route. Carry its passengers from start through the interval before end. At a shared location, drop-offs happen before pickups. Decide whether the vehicle can complete every trip without exceeding capacity.

examples.explanation: The first passengers leave before the next pickup.
Four passengers overlap between locations 3 and 5.
The trip can span the full location range.

constraints: 1–1000 trips. Each passenger count is in [1,100]. 0 ≤ start < end ≤ 1000. 1 ≤ capacity ≤ 100000.
hints: Conceptual: Only pickup and drop-off locations can change occupancy.
Directional: Record each trip as two occupancy changes.
Implementation: Add its count at start and subtract it at end. Scan the cumulative changes and reject any load above capacity.
complexityAnalysis: O(n+U) time and O(U) auxiliary space, where U=1001 route locations.
